target.title: fix(memory): bound unsignaled remote HTTP with default timeoutMs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory remote HTTP (`withRemoteHttpResponse`) only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Embedding batch / `postJson` callers often omit a signal (Google/OpenAI/Voyage upload and status polls), so a peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could hang the Gateway forever. Idle body caps never start until headers arrive. Callers that pass a cancellation-only `AbortSignal` (no deadline) had the same hang risk when the wrapper treated any signal as a reason to skip the transport floor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Install a shared hang floor via existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs`, and compose it with any caller `AbortSignal`:

- Default: `MEMORY_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` = 120s (aligned with memory remote batch budgets so large uploads are not clamped below established policy)
- Explicit `timeoutMs` override still wins
- Caller `AbortSignal` is always forwarded; `fetchWithSsrFGuard` / `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` compose cancellation with the floor so cancellation-only signals cannot disable the hang bound

Also forward optional `timeoutMs` through `postJson` so production JSON POST callers can override the floor without reimplementing the wrapper.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled (or cancellation-only-signaled) memory remote HTTP could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream.

**After:** Requests fail closed after 120s by default (`TimeoutError` / `request timed out`), including when a caller supplies a cancellation-only `AbortSignal`. Explicit `timeoutMs` and earlier caller aborts still win.

## Evidence

- Changed: `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.ts`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.ts`
- Production path under test: `withRemoteHttpResponse` (shared by `postJson` / batch-upload / provider embedding batches) against a real local `node:http` server that never writes headers
- Regression: `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.test.ts`, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.test.ts`

### Caller-path hang proof (Vitest)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

**Commands run:**
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/remote-http.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/post-json.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**Before fix:**
Unsignaled `withRemoteHttpResponse` / `postJson` forwarded no `timeoutMs` to `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, so a peer that accepted TCP and never returned headers could hang until process restart. Supplying a cancellation-only `AbortSignal` also skipped the floor.

**After fix:**
With a short `timeoutMs` override (stand-in for the 120s production floor), hung POST/GET requests reject with `TimeoutError: request timed out` whether or not a cancellation-only caller signal is present. Mocked calls assert the default floor is always `MEMORY_REMOTE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` unless an explicit override is set, and that caller signals are still forwarded for composition.

**Evidence after fix:**
```text

 ✓ |unit-fast| ... > honours an explicit timeoutMs override even when a caller signal is present
 ✓ |unit-fast| ... > times out hung remote responses when caller omits signal 101ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| ... > times out hung remote responses when caller supplies a cancellation-only signal 84ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| ... > times out hung POST bodies shaped like postJson callers 84ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 6.05s
```

**What was not tested:**
Live remote embedding provider endpoints; full 120s production floor duration (proof uses an 80ms override against a local hung server).
